unmapped_findings: Table 7 (b0056): EDS for Al and Mn in 12Al-20Mn-1C tempered at 800 °C (wt%, Min/Mean/Max). Al: δ 11.0/11.9/13.6, γ 5.7/7.8/9.9, k 10.3/10.8/11.9. Mn: δ 15.2/17.9/20.8, γ 20.3/23.6/27.6, k 21.9/23.9/25.5. Al is highest in δ-ferrite and lowest in γ; Mn is lowest in δ and highest in γ and k.

For the 12Al-20Mn-1C alloy tempered at 800 °C the cellular-transformed fractions were reported as predominant over the spinodal decomposed fractions, attributed to lower Mn-γ stability (text b0113, Fig. 13(b)); Fig. 13 was captioned for panels (a) 9Al-10Mn-1C, (b) 12Al-20Mn-1C and (c) 12Al-30Mn-1C but only the panel containing 9Al-10Mn-1C was supplied.

Internal inconsistency in the paper regarding the nano-sized κ-carbide morphology of 12Al-20Mn-1C at 800 °C: the Results text (b0057) and Fig. 8(c,d) assign the 'densest and thickest configuration with proper cuboidal morphology' to 12Al-20Mn-1C, whereas the Conclusions (b0121/b0122) attribute 'medium dense and thin needle-like κ-carbides' to 12Al + 20Mn and the 'most dense and thickest nano-sized cuboidal κ-carbides' to 12Al + 30Mn.

The inter-lamellar spacing of the 800 °C tempered 12Al-20Mn-1C structure is described only qualitatively as high/wide (b0053), stated to be consistent with the hardening effects despite the high spacing; Table 9 lists 'Wide' inter-lamellar spacing for 12Al-10Mn-1C at 800 °C (401 → 399 HV), not for this sample.

No tensile, ductility, density, thermal, electrical or magnetic property data are reported specifically for the 12Al-20Mn-1C 800 °C tempered sample; the reported mechanical data are Vickers macro-hardness only.

The paper notes (b0114) that higher hardness is related to higher tensile properties and that thick precipitates formed by spinodal decomposition are associated with brittleness, but no tensile/ductility values are given for this sample.

Fig. 7 caption (b0052) labels the product as 'κ + γ Lamellae in 12Al-20Mn-1C at 800 °C', while the citing text describes the same structure as κ-carbide + α + residual-γ lamellae produced by cellular transformation plus spinodal decomposition.
